verdict.line: You lose if you trade into his dash-in burst before level 6; you win if you poke with Q and scale into Heartsteel/Thornmail past level 11.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Fury-gated empowered W and his E gap-close give him the stronger burst and engage pattern through the first several levels, which is why Tahm sits at only 44.1% here over 227 games despite a 50.7% overall top-lane record. Tahm's real leverage is his 900-range Q (Tongue Lash) poke and the stun he builds through An Acquired Taste stacks — he wins by refusing Renekton's dash-in windows and fighting only on his own terms.

theirWindow.what: He dashes in to trade — possibly with an empowered 3-hit, 1.5s-stun W if he's above 50 Fury — then dashes back out. Don't feed him free pokes into this window; just eat the trade and reset.

yourWindow.what: He has no gap close or retreat. Step up and freely land Q (900 range, slows and applies an Acquired Taste stack) into autos — he cannot punish the poke or run from it.

Fury-empowered Q/W raise his trade damage
R (Devour) gives you a bailout/kill tool

start.why: Taken in 69.6% of games (38.5% WR) and the better answer to Renekton's early auto/Q sustain poke than Doran's Helm.

boots.why: Run in 70.3% of games (40.8% WR) — flattens the physical-damage autos he uses to build Fury toward his empowered abilities.

core.why: First item in the highest-winrate path for this matchup (60% WR, 11.3% pick) — stacks health that both scales your passive bonus damage and blunts his burst.
Second item in the same 60% WR path, keeping you durable through his Fury-empowered trade windows.
Caps the path at 60% WR over 15 games — directly punishes his auto-attack-reliant Fury generation.

situational.when: he's auto-attacking you aggressively pre-6 to snowball Fury for his empowered W/Q
you need more frontline sustain than Thornmail alone provides
the enemy team's damage profile shifts magic-heavy later

runes.keystoneWhy: Run in the 49.3%-pick page (48% WR) — the sustain procs off autos during your Q-poke pattern, which is exactly how you're meant to fight this lane.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is the standard pick (46.4% WR, 60.1% pick) for this lane. If you want to directly blunt his all-in burst windows, Exhaust+Flash has the highest measured winrate (52.4%) in a smaller sample.

playing.title: Poke, don't trade
playing.detail: Lean on Q (Tongue Lash, 900 range) to harass him on cooldown while farming — its reach outclasses his 325/300/450-range kit, so you can tag him without stepping into stun range.

playing.title: Hold Q for his dash window
playing.detail: Keep distance while last-hitting and land Q the instant he closes with E — this slows the all-in, applies an Acquired Taste stack, and starts your sustain proc.

playing.title: Track Fury before you shield
playing.detail: Above 50 Fury his W becomes a 3-hit, 1.5s stun that destroys shields outright — never pop E (Thick Skin)'s shield into that version; bait it out on a low-Fury W instead.

playing.title: Bank the stun-stacks combo
playing.detail: Build 3 Acquired Taste stacks through Q poke and autos, then land a 4th Tongue Lash to stun him and consume the stacks — follow immediately with R (Devour) if he's isolated for a solo kill.

playing.title: Punish his E cooldown
playing.detail: Slice and Dice sits at 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s — whenever it's down he has no gap close or retreat, so step up and freely trade.

playing.title: Respect the level 2 spike
playing.detail: His rank-1 W stun plus Q sustain makes level 2 dangerous before your own W (Abyssal Dive) is up to disengage — play passive until you have it.

playing.title: Play for scaling, not lane kills
playing.detail: At 44.1% head-to-head you aren't expected to win lane outright — farm through the poke, hit 6 for Devour pressure, and take over once Heartsteel and Thornmail come online.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all winrate/pick/sample numbers above are measured from live games on the current patch (OP.GG); the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are this brief's own tactical read.

stats.opponentTip: Renekton will use (E) to close in, deal damage, and retreat afterwards using (E). Keep some distance while farming and use [Q] when he closes in to attack him with basic attacks. Try to hit him with [Q] when he is farming as well.
